newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar enters Year of Ox with lower close.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar enters Year of Ox with lower close.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar started the lunar Year of the Ox by finishing sharply lower on Tuesday on mounting expectations that it should depreciate to reflect the U.S. dollar's global rise, dealers said.
In the first day of trading after a five-day Chinese lunar new year holiday, the local dollar dipped to an intraday low of T$27.549 before recovering slightly to end at T$27.540.
Last Wednesday, on the eve of the holiday, the Taiwan dollar had closed at T$27.508 to the U.S. dollar.
Tuesday turnover through dealers was a heavy US$273.5 million.

The slide reflected the dissipation of annual pre-holiday cash demand as well as a widespread feeling that the Taiwan dollar was overvalued -- a feeling that intensified after the central bank hinted it would not oppose a devaluation.
"As exporters' pre-holiday U.S. dollar sales formally came to an end, the Taiwan dollar is now dominated by U.S. dollar's overseas trend," said one dealer at a foreign bank.

The central bank said before the holiday break that the Taiwan dollar "in theory" should reflect the U.S. dollar's prolonged overseas rise -- a statement widely interpreted in the market as a call for a depreciation.
Dealers expected the Taiwan dollar gradually to test support at T$27.60 in the near term, though analysts said there was only limited room for a more significant depreciation.
Chinatrust Commercial Bank chief economist Daniel Chen told Reuters by telephone that he did not expect the Taiwan dollar to fall below T$28 to the U.S. dollar in 1997.
"The central bank should let the Taiwan dollar depreciate in response to the strong U.S. dollar overseas as we don't have inflation worries due to negative import price growth in 1996," Chen said.
"Letting the Taiwan dollar depreciate also will help exports, but because of likely persistent inflows of foreign funds for the stock market, it will at most fall to T$28 this year," Chen added.
A trading range of T$27.48-56 was seen for Wednesday.
